items.title: Hitachi Energy CoreTec Product
items.summary: View CSAF Summary Hitachi Energy is aware of OS command injection and Dirty Frag vulnerabilities that affect CoreTec product versions listed in this document. Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could result in impact on confidentiality, integrity and availability of the product. Please refer to the Recommended Immediate Actions for information about the mitigation/remediation. The following versions of Hitachi Energy CoreTec Product are affected: CoreTec5 vers:CoreTec5/<=3.4.0, 5.0.0 (CVE-2026-13162, CVE-2026-43284) CoreTec4 vers:CoreTec4/<=3.4.0 (CVE-2026-13162) CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 8.8 Hitachi Energy CoreTec5 2 Vulnerabilities Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection'), Write-what-where Condition Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Energy Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: Switzerland Vulnerabilities Expand All + CVE-2026-13162 An OS command vulnerability exists in CoreTec product that allows authenticated users with certain roles to execute arbitrary system commands with full control over the device. The vulnerability exists in the configuration daemon's time synchronization handler, which is responsible for setting the system timezone. When processing timezone configuration updates, the daemon constructs a shell command by concatenating user-supplied input without any sanitization or validation. Read More 2 Affected Products CoreTec5 versions 3.4.0 and prior Product Status: fixed, known_affected, recommended Remediations Vendor fix Update to CoreTec5 version 5.0.0 CoreTec4 versions 3.4.0 and prior Product Status: fixed, known_affected, recommended Remediations Vendor fix Upgrade to CoreTec5 version 5.0.0 Mitigation Follow general mitigation factors Additional Metrics Relevant CWE: CWE-78 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection') CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 7.5 HIGH CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H 4.0 7.7 HIGH CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N View CVE Details CVE-2026-43284 A vulnerability exists in the IPsec ESP subsystem (esp4) of the Linux kernel used in CoreTec5 that allows a local unprivileged user to escalate privileges to root. The flaw exists in how the kernel handles memory pages when processing ESP encrypted network packets. An attacker can craft a packet that causes the kernel to decrypt data directly into memory pages it does not own, including cached copies of privileged operating system binaries. When one of those binaries is executed, the attacker's injected code runs with root privileges. In CoreTec5, the vulnerable ESP component is compiled in kernel as a built-in and is present at boot time allowing a local user to exploit it. Read More 3 Affected Products CoreTec5 versions 3.4.0 and prior Product Status: fixed, known_affected, recommended Remediations Vendor fix Update to CoreTec5 version 5.0.0 CoreTec4 versions 3.4.0 and prior Product Status: fixed, known_affected, recommended Remediations CoreTec5 versions 3.4.0 and prior Product Status: fixed, known_affected, recommended Remediations Vendor fix Update to CoreTec5 version 5.0.0 Additional Metrics Relevant CWE: CWE-123 Write-what-where Condition CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 8.8 HIGH CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H View CVE Details Acknowledgments Ritesh Kumar Kalle, Subhojeet Mukherjee, Hishamudeen of the Cybersecurity Research group, Hitachi India R&D Center reported these vulnerabilities to CISA. For contact information, see https://www.hitachienergy.com/contact-us/ for Hitachi Energy contact-centers. General Mitigation Factors Recommended security practices and firewall configurations can help protect a process control network from attacks that originate from outside the network. Such practices include that process control systems are physically protected from direct access by unauthorized personnel, have no direct connections to the Internet, and are separated from other networks by means of a firewall system that has a minimal number of ports exposed, and others that have to be evaluated case by case. Process control systems should not be used for Internet surfing, instant messaging, or receiving e-mails. Portable computers and removable storage media should be carefully scanned for viruses before they are connected to a control system. Proper password policies and processes should be followed. Additional information on Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity Best Practices can be found in the Hitachi Energy “Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity Best Practices” Cybersecurity Notification. [1] SSVC SSVCv2/E:N/A:N/2026-10-26T15:17:24Z/ Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet . Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices. CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures. CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics . Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies . CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets . Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies . Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents. items.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.summary: CISA has added two new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2026-97229 GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition Integer Overflow or Wraparound vulnerability CVE-2026-76418 Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software and Cisco Secure FTD Software Unchecked Return Value to NULL Pointer Dereference Vulnerability These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria . Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form . Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

items.title: Webinar: How to Build AI Threat Readiness Into Your Security Operations
items.summary: Security teams have spent years trying to detect threats faster. AI is changing the harder part: how much time defenders have left to act. Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet . Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices. CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures. CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics . Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies . CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets . Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies . Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents. items.title: EPICS Base
items.summary: View CSAF Summary Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to cause a denial-of-service condition, corrupt memory, disclose sensitive information, or potentially execute arbitrary code. The following versions of EPICS Base are affected: EPICS Base release <=7.0.10 (CVE-2026-114595, CVE-2026-114596, CVE-2026-114597, CVE-2026-114598) CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 9.8 The EPICS Community EPICS Base release 3 Vulnerabilities Integer Overflow or Wraparound, Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency, Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion') Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: Global Vulnerabilities Expand All + CVE-2026-114595 In EPICS Base release 7.0.10 and prior, an integer overflow in network request processing can cause memory to be allocated with an incorrect size. Subsequent handling of attacker supplied data may result in memory corruption, denial of service, or potential remote code execution. items.title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
items.summary: CISA has added one new vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2026-114625 Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator SQL Injection Vulnerability This type of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and poses significant risks to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria . Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form . Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

items.title: Siemens PSS(R)SINCAL

An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to cause a system crash, resulting in a denial-of-service condition. This affects PSS SINCAL only when configured to use the legacy WibuKey dongle license type. Siemens is actively preparing updates and recommends applicable mitigations for products where patches are currently unavailable. General Recommendations Operators of critical power systems (e.g. TSOs or DSOs) worldwide are usually required by regulations to build resilience into the power grids by applying multi-level redundant secondary protection schemes. It is therefore recommended that the operators check whether appropriate resilient protection measures are in place. The risk of cyber incidents impacting the grid's reliability can thus be minimized by virtue of the grid design. Siemens strongly recommends applying the provided security updates using the corresponding tooling and documented procedures made available with the product. If supported by the product, an automated means to apply the security updates across multiple product instances may be used. Siemens strongly recommends prior validation of any security update before being applied, and supervision by trained staff of the update process in the target environment. As a general security measure Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access with appropriate mechanisms (e.g. firewalls, segmentation, VPN). It is advised to configure the environment according to our operational guidelines in order to run the devices in a protected IT environment. items.summary: View CSAF Summary RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW contains multiple vulnerabilities that could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary SQL commands on the underlying database, retrieve sensitive administrative credentials, escalate privileges, and perform unauthorized operations such as modifying system configurations or causing a denial of service. Siemens has released a new version for RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW and recommends to update to the latest version. The following versions of Siemens RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW are affected: RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW vers:intdot/<6.0 (CVE-2026-89196, CVE-2026-89197, CVE-2026-89198, CVE-2026-89199, CVE-2026-89200, CVE-2026-89201, CVE-2026-89202, CVE-2026-89203, CVE-2026-89204, CVE-2026-89205, CVE-2026-89206) CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 8.8 Siemens RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW 4 Vulnerabilities Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection'), Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key, Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data, Client-Side Enforcement of Server-Side Security Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: Germany Vulnerabilities Expand All + CVE-2026-89196 Affected devices do not properly validate or sanitize input in facility names processed during the Bulk Import/Export workflow. This could allow an authenticated attacker with specific privileges to execute arbitrary SQL commands on the underlying database. General Recommendations As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity Additional Resources For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories Terms of Use The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use. Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet . Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices. CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures. CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics . Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies . CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets . Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies . Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents. items.title: Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 Devices
items.summary: View CSAF Summary Nozomi Networks has published information on vulnerabilities in Nozomi Guardian/CMC. This advisory lists the related Siemens Industrial products affected by these vulnerabilities. Siemens recommends to contact customer support to receive patch and update information. The following versions of Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 Devices are affected: RUGGEDCOM APE1808 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-33387, CVE-2026-33388, CVE-2026-33389, CVE-2026-33391, CVE-2026-33920) CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 7.5 Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 4 Vulnerabilities Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine, Incorrect Authorization, Lack of Administrator Control over Security, Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: Germany Vulnerabilities Expand All + CVE-2026-33387 A template injection vulnerability was discovered in the Dashboards functionality due to improper validation of an input parameter. An authenticated user with the required privileges can define a dashboard containing a malicious payload, or a victim can be socially engineered into importing a malicious dashboard. When the victim views or imports the dashboard, the payload executes in their browser context, allowing the attacker to modify application data or disrupt application availability. Read More 1 Affected Product RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMC Product Status: known_affected Remediations Vendor fix Contact customer support to receive patch and update information Additional Metrics Relevant CWE: CWE-1336 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 4.6 MEDIUM CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:L View CVE Details CVE-2026-33388 An access control vulnerability was discovered in the Credentials Manager functionality due to insufficient validation of user privileges. A remote authenticated user with limited privileges can view a limited subset of the available entries in the Credentials Manager. The actual credential values are not directly visible, but the user can delete entries or edit their properties. An attacker who deletes or edits an entry can disrupt authentication for dependent devices, and one who manipulates an entry's configuration may be able to indirectly obtain the credentials. Read More 2 Affected Products RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMC Product Status: known_affected Remediations Vendor fix Contact customer support to receive patch and update information RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMC Product Status: known_affected Remediations Vendor fix Contact customer support to receive patch and update information Additional Metrics Relevant CWE: CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 7.4 HIGH CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:L View CVE Details CVE-2026-33389 An improper certificate/host key validation vulnerability was discovered in the Smart Polling functionality, which established encrypted connections to target devices without validating the remote host's identity, and no option was provided to enable it. A man-in-the-middle attacker positioned between a sensor and a polled device can, during a polling session, impersonate the device and intercept the communication, including the credentials used to access it. The captured credentials can then be replayed to authenticate against the device itself or against other devices sharing the same credentials, allowing the attacker to access and tamper with the device's data and to disrupt its operations. An authenticated user with limited privileges can remotely bypass the intended access control of the web management interface and modify the Smart Polling discovery configuration. Read More 4 Affected Products RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMC Product Status: known_affected Remediations Vendor fix Contact customer support to receive patch and update information RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMC Product Status: known_affected Remediations Vendor fix Contact customer support to receive patch and update information RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMC Product Status: known_affected Remediations Vendor fix Contact customer support to receive patch and update information RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMC Product Status: known_affected Remediations Vendor fix Contact customer support to receive patch and update information Additional Metrics Relevant CWE: CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 5.4 MEDIUM CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:L View CVE Details CVE-2026-33920 A cross-site request forgery vulnerability was discovered in the login functionality (both standard and SAML) due to missing validation of the anti-CSRF token. Any operation performed by the victim in this state is attributed to the attacker's account, compromising the integrity of the audit trail. items.title: Siemens Industrial Edge App Publisher
items.summary: View CSAF Summary The Industrial Edge App Publisher contains a vulnerability chain involving improper certificate validation and the rendering of unescaped data from backend responses. These issues can be combined to allow an attacker on the network to impersonate the management server and execute arbitrary code (RCE) on the local machine through Node.js integration. Siemens has released an update for the Industrial Edge App Publisher and recommends to update to the latest version. The following versions of Siemens Industrial Edge App Publisher are affected: Industrial Edge App Publisher vers:intdot/<1.27.9 (CVE-2026-78556, CVE-2026-78557) CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 8.3 Siemens Industrial Edge App Publisher 2 Vulnerabilities Improper Certificate Validation, Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: Germany Vulnerabilities Expand All + CVE-2026-78556 The affected software does not properly validate the server certificate when initiating a TLS connection. This allows an attacker to intercept and relay communication (Man-in-the-Middle attack) and to spoof a trusted entity by interfering in the communication path between the client and the intended server. Read More 1 Affected Product Industrial Edge App Publisher < V1.27.9 Product Status: known_affected Remediations Vendor fix Update to V1.27.9 or later version Additional Metrics Relevant CWE: CWE-295 Improper Certificate Validation CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 7.4 HIGH CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N View CVE Details CVE-2026-78557 The application fails to properly sanitize or escape data received from the backend before rendering it in the user interface. items.title: Siemens WinCC
items.summary: View CSAF Summary Multiple SIMATIC WinCC versions are affected by a database privilege escalation vulnerability that could allow an authenticated user with access to the database to execute commands on the underlying host system. Siemens has released new versions for several affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions. Siemens is preparing further fixes and recommends mitigations for products where fixes are not or not yet available. The following versions of Siemens WinCC are affected: SIMATIC WinCC V7.5 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-59241) SIMATIC WinCC V8.0 vers:intdot/<8.0.0.11 (CVE-2026-59241) SIMATIC WinCC V8.1 vers:intdot/<8.1.7 (CVE-2026-59241) CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 8.8 Siemens SIMATIC WinCC V7.5 1 Vulnerability Incorrect Privilege Assignment Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: Germany Vulnerabilities CVE-2026-59241 The affected application does not sufficiently restrict the permissions assigned to a database role. This could allow an authenticated remote attacker with database access to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary commands on the host system where SIMATIC WinCC is installed, potentially leading to a compromise of the system. items.title: Siemens Industrial Edge Device Kit
items.summary: View CSAF Summary Users of Industrial Edge Devices are advised to consult the respective Security Advisories for their devices (for Siemens Industrial Edge devices see Additional Information). Industrial Edge Device Kit contains multiple path traversal vulnerabilities that could facilitate an authenticated remote attacker to access sensitive internal information. Siemens has released new versions for several affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions. Siemens recommends specific countermeasures for products where fixes are not, or not yet available. The following versions of Siemens Industrial Edge Device Kit are affected: Industrial Edge Device Kit - arm64 V1.10 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-44414, CVE-2026-44415) Industrial Edge Device Kit - arm64 V1.11 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-44414, CVE-2026-44415) Industrial Edge Device Kit - General Recommendations As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity Additional Resources For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories Terms of Use The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use. Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet . Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices. CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures. CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics . Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies . CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets . Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies . Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents. items.title: Siemens APOGEE, TALON and Desigo PXC/PXM Products

items.title: Managing AI Token Consumption for Operational Resilience
items.summary: CISA, the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre), and partners are releasing joint guidance, Managing AI Token Consumption for Operational Resilience , to help organizations understand and manage token usage in support of operations. As organizations adopt third-party super intelligence (SI) services, token-based usage models can affect cost, performance, and access to critical services. Unmanaged token consumption may contribute to rising and unpredictable costs, reduced service availability, degraded performance, token exhaustion, and denial-of-tokens or denial-of-wallet attacks. The guidance outlines practical steps organizations can take to prioritize token allocation, design efficient workflows, improve user prompting practices, leverage caching and reusable context, optimize data before submission, and monitor token consumption over time. Critical infrastructure owners and operators can use this guidance to identify mission-critical functions that depend on SI, understand service provider and operational dependencies, and plan for reduced SI availability during outages, incidents, or periods of high demand. Cyber defenders can also use the guidance to manage SI-enabled cyber defense workflows while maintaining human oversight, governance, and strong cybersecurity fundamentals.

This could lead to a memory corruption issue. We recommend upgrading to version 3.50.2 or above. Read More 1 Affected Product RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0 Product Status: known_affected Remediations Vendor fix Update to V6.0 or later version Additional Metrics Relevant CWE: CWE-197 Numeric Truncation Error CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 7.7 HIGH CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:H/A:L View CVE Details CVE-2025-70873 An information disclosure issue in the zipfileInflate function in the zipfile extension in SQLite v3.51.1 and earlier allows attackers to obtain heap memory via supplying a crafted ZIP file. Read More 2 Affected Products RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0 Product Status: known_affected Remediations Vendor fix Update to V6.0 or later version RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0 Product Status: known_affected Remediations Vendor fix Update to V6.0 or later version Additional Metrics Relevant CWE: CWE-244 Improper Clearing of Heap Memory Before Release ('Heap Inspection') CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 7.5 HIGH CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N View CVE Details CVE-2025-71316 SQLite 'sqldiff.exe' does not securely handle the way the Microsoft Windows C runtime converts Unicode characters to ANSI codepages. An attacker could use the '-L' option to load an arbitrary DLL with a crafted command line argument string that results in command line file arguments being misinterpreted as command line options. Fixed on or around 2025-12-26. Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents. items.title: Kiloview E3 NDI Encoder
items.summary: View CSAF Summary Successful exploitation of this these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to fully compromise the device. The following versions of Kiloview E3 NDI Encoder are affected: E3 Firmware <1.30 (CVE-2026-109122, CVE-2026-111100, CVE-2026-96616, CVE-2026-105265, CVE-2026-110491, CVE-2026-107861, CVE-2026-110243, CVE-2026-92450, CVE-2026-110825) CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 9.9 Kiloview E3 Firmware 6 Vulnerabilities Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection'), Missing Authentication for Critical Function, Insufficient Session Expiration, Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal'), NULL Pointer Dereference, Use of Hard-coded Credentials Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Communications, Information Technology Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: China Vulnerabilities Expand All + CVE-2026-109122 The network management service on affected Kiloview E3 NDI encoder firmware fails to sanitize one field used when configuring static routes via the web management API. An authenticated web user with permission to configure static routes can exploit this to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root, and the malicious configuration persists across reboots. Successful exploitation could result in full device compromise, including exposure of stored credentials and cryptographic material. items.summary: View CSAF Summary Multiple vulnerabilities have been identified in the additional GNU/Linux subsystem of the SIMATIC S7-1500 TM MFP V1.1.1. Siemens is preparing fixes and recommends specific mitigations for products where fixes are not or not yet available. The following versions of Siemens SIMATIC S7-1500 TM MFP are affected: SIMATIC S7-1500 TM MFP - GNU/Linux subsystem vers:all/* CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 10 Siemens SIMATIC S7-1500 TM MFP - GNU/Linux subsystem 377 Vulnerabilities Access of Uninitialized Pointer, Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow'), Deadlock, Detection of Error Condition Without Action, Double Free, Expired Pointer Dereference, Heap-based Buffer Overflow, Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection'), Improper Control of a Resource Through its Lifetime, Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency, Improper Handling of Missing Special Element, Improper Handling of Structural Elements, Improper Input Validation, Improper Locking, Improper Resource Locking, Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer, Improper Update of Reference Count, Improper Validation of Array Index, Improper Validation of Consistency within Input, Improper Validation of Specified Index, Position, or Offset in Input, Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input, Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input, Incorrect Synchronization, Integer Overflow or Wraparound, Integer Underflow (Wrap or Wraparound), Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop'), Missing Default Case in Multiple Condition Expression, Missing Initialization of Resource, Missing Lock Check, Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime, Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime, Multiple Locks of a Critical Resource, NULL Pointer Dereference, Operation on a Resource after Expiration or Release, Out-of-bounds Read, Out-of-bounds Write, Plaintext Storage of a Password, Release of Invalid Pointer or Reference, Return of Wrong Status Code, Signal Handler Race Condition, Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition, Unchecked Return Value, Use After Free, Use of Incorrect Operator, Use of Uninitialized Resource, Write-what-where Condition Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: Germany Vulnerabilities Expand All + CVE-2023-52927 In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: netfilter: allow exp not to be removed in nf_ct_find_expectation Currently nf_conntrack_in() calling nf_ct_find_expectation() will remove the exp from the hash table. However, in some scenario, we expect the exp not to be removed when the created ct will not be confirmed, like in OVS and TC conntrack in the following patches. This patch allows exp not to be removed by setting IPS_CONFIRMED in the status of the tmpl. General Recommendations As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity Additional Resources For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories Terms of Use The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use. Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet . Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices. CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures. CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics . Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies . CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets . Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies . Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents. items.title: UAE Transitions 50% of Government Services to Agentic AI
items.summary: The United Arab Emirates says it's creating a foundation of security and safety as it transforms its public service footprint.

items.title: TiDB Breach Exposes Flawed Cloud Security Assumptions
items.summary: Cloud providers may be storing sensitive customer data, without either party knowing it. But when a provider is breached, the unseen information comes to light.

items.title: Compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates
items.summary: Cisco Talos is aware of eight intermediate certificates belonging to the intermediate certificate authority, eMudhra.

items.title: Marvell, Microsoft & Oracle Work to Standardize Data Center Hardware Security
items.summary: The effort is aimed at standardizing a NIST FIPS 140-3 Level 3 integrated HSM for cloud and hyperscale data center infrastructure.

items.title: Cloud Security Alliance Survey Finds Data Loss Prevention Often Detects Data Loss Only After It Happens
items.summary: Research finds that, among respondents experiencing data loss, only 16% said DLP blocked their most significant incidents before data left the organization.

items.title: 'PHP2Shell' Bugs Signal Red Alert for Security Industry
items.summary: Security teams are scrambling to remediate two critical PHP vulnerabilities following leaked details and reports of exploitation attempts.

items.title: AI-driven, large-scale nation-state campaign using ARTEX enables supply chain compromise
items.summary: Storm-0940 used ARTEX agentic AI to accelerate a ConnectWise supply chain compromise, enabling application credential abuse across Microsoft 365 environments. The post AI-driven, large-scale nation-state campaign using ARTEX enables supply chain compromise appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

items.title: OVHcloud GitHub Compromise Tied to GlassWorm Threat Actors
items.summary: A developer's GitHub account that was compromised several months earlier was used to push malicious code to unsuspecting users.

items.title: Optiv Launches CyberBOT Cybersecurity Awareness Training Program
items.summary: Hands-on sessions provide educators, nonprofits, and community leaders with an accessible resource to foster year-round cyber awareness and build more resilient communities.

items.title: Survey Finds High-Profile Executives Feel Untouchable as Digital Exposure Turns Into Physical Risk
items.summary: 360 Privacy finds more than 8 in 10 security and wealth professionals say cybersecurity and physical security can no longer be separated.

items.title: Two critical RCEs in PHP core
items.summary: Two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in PHP core could have implications across its wider ecosystem. Talos has published a blog to explain what we know so far, and details the Snort coverage available, including rules in the Community Ruleset.

items.title: Introducing full transaction detection for Cloudflare WAF
items.summary: Cloudflare's web application firewall can now correlate an HTTP request with its response. Full transaction detection helps every customer find successful exploits, data exposure, and risky misconfigurations that request-only inspection can miss.

items.title: “Next Exploit Opportunities”: How a Threat Actor Used AI to Help Plan and Execute Multiple Types of Cybercrime Activities
items.summary: An investigation into a threat actor bypassing AI safety controls to coordinate credential theft, VoIP fraud planning, and database exfiltration. The post “Next Exploit Opportunities”: How a Threat Actor Used AI to Help Plan and Execute Multiple Types of Cybercrime Activities appeared first on Unit 42 .

items.title: Cloudflare deploys protections against php2shell vulnerability
items.summary: Cloudflare has deployed default web application firewall (WAF) protections for newly disclosed PHP vulnerabilities before public disclosure. The rules use request and response signals to stop exploit attempts and prevent exposed data from reaching attackers.

items.title: Decades-Old Windows Utility Powers Modern ClickFix Attack
items.summary: The attack uses malicious Google search results related to Amazon and leverages the "finger" utility to launch a CAPTCHA that installs malware, including the Lumma stealer.

items.title: Parasitizing trust: How legitimate infrastructure becomes a delivery pipeline for attackers
items.summary: Adversaries are turning the tools businesses trust into delivery mechanisms for malicious activity. Cisco Talos observed abuse of more than 25 legitimate platforms over the past year, exploiting the built-in trust of collaboration, file-sharing, payment and other services to reach their targets.

items.title: 8 eMudhra certificates are compromised. Here's what you need to know
items.summary: Following the discovery that eight eMudhra intermediate certificates use weak keys, Cloudflare is deploying mitigations and releasing client updates. We explain the impact, our response, and what customers and developers should do next.

items.title: Tech Giants Block eMudhra Certificates Tied to 8 Compromised Keys
items.summary: Google, Mozilla, Apple, the Go project and others moved swiftly to block the affected certificates from the Indian CA, though it's unclear how the keys were compromised.

items.title: Active Exploitation of May 2026 PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 (Updated October 20)
items.summary: Ransomware operators including Spikey Scorpius (aka Qilin) and Tarnished Scorpius (aka Inc) are exploiting PAN-OS vulnerability CVE-2026-0257. The post Active Exploitation of May 2026 PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 (Updated October 20) appeared first on Unit 42 .

items.title: Ex-OpenAI Engineer Detained After Planting Secret Recorder at HQ
items.summary: The perp, who has Saudi ties, was arrested for allegedly bugging an OpenAI conference room, highlighting a preventable insider threat vector.

items.title: Close Identity Gaps in Software Development Before Unleashing AI
items.summary: Artificial intelligence is complicating security in the software development life cycle, but a Dark Reading roundtable found collaboration, better identity visibility, and reduced testing costs offer CISOs a way ahead.

items.title: There's only so much code: the rise in vulnerability numbers
items.summary: The September Microsoft Patch Tuesday release included 975 vulnerability advisories. This month, 1,415 vulnerabilities were just dropped. Compared to a pre-June average of 100 a month, that increase is staggering. Where did they come from? And what does the future look like?

items.title: Hackers Abuse AI Pen-Test Tool Cairn to Automate Massive Attack Spree
items.summary: A Chinese-speaking attacker has compromised hundreds of websites across the globe, looting from big fish like John Deere, SharkNinja, and engine manufacturer Cummins.

items.title: Researchers Infiltrate Microsoft Tech Support Scam Operation
items.summary: A large-scale scam operation impersonating Microsoft uses a malicious traffic distribution system (TDS) run by a Russian organization and abuses thousands of Cloudflare links.

items.title: 'AdFection' Turns Ad Impressions Into Zero-Click Spyware Delivery
items.summary: Spyware vendors are exploiting targeted ad bidding in the digital ecosystem to identify and track individuals and organizations of interest.

items.title: ConnectWise Disables Cloud Backups Amid Concerns for Downstream MSPs
items.summary: Researchers say attackers authenticated into Microsoft 365 tenants using ConnectWise credentials; ConnectWise says customer impact remains unconfirmed.

items.title: OnlyFans Copyright Takedowns Expose Compromised Websites
items.summary: Copyright takedown requests tied to OnlyFans and other adult content creators are revealing how attackers exploit vulnerable university and government websites to manipulate search results. UpGuard's Greg Pollock explains what universities, government websites, and security teams need to think about next.

items.title: The Evolving Cybersecurity Lexicon: Vulnerability Discovery to Resilience
items.summary: An industry-wide, laser focus on vulnerabilities has left cybersecurity teams without enough room to strategize for resilience.

items.title: Agents are your newest insiders. Security must move at their speed.
items.summary: New capabilities in Microsoft 365 E7 and Project Perception help organizations contain agent risk and adapt protection continuously. The post Agents are your newest insiders. Security must move at their speed. appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

items.title: Beyond the patch: Protecting your NetScaler gateway against future vulnerabilities
items.summary: CVE-2026-88771 lets attackers run commands on NetScaler Gateway before anyone signs in. Patching takes time most teams don't have, so the sign-in decision has to move in front of the vulnerable code.

items.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support Zero-Day Continues Trend of Exploited Edge Bugs
items.summary: Ivanti, Cisco, and Palo Alto Networks all had vulnerabilities in edge devices come under fire this week. Now BeyondTrust joins the group.

items.title: Managing open-weight model risk in enterprise deployments
items.summary: New whitepaper from Microsoft and NVIDIA helps enterprises manage open-weight AI model risks with a shared taxonomy, evaluations, and controls. The post Managing open-weight model risk in enterprise deployments appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

items.title: Continuous accountability for Verified bots
items.summary: Identity alone doesn't guarantee a bot will behave responsibly. We are introducing a system to continuously evaluate whether Verified bots honor site preferences, like robots.txt and HTTP 429s, ensuring they remain accountable over time.
